description: “With God as my witness / … blood on his hands” — Immediate God/Devil opposition. “Blood on his hands” is both literal sinister imagery and the idiom for being responsible for others' suffering/deaths.

“Something so familiar about him” — Interesting because the Devil isn't presented as completely alien. Temptation feels familiar—possibly because what he's offering already exists as a desire inside Ren. Not confirmed, but a good observation.
“Looking fresh to death” — Common idiom meaning extremely stylish, but here he's literally looking at the Devil/death-associated figure. Nice contextual double meaning.

“I caught his eye and then I felt like I was drowning” — The encounter immediately removes Ren's control. Later the Devil promises to free him from pain, despite already being the thing pulling him under.

“Standing at the crossroads” — The big one: the Robert Johnson crossroads legend, where Johnson supposedly traded his soul to the Devil for musical ability. Especially appropriate because Ren performs the song as blues. Ren confirmed the crossroads concept.
“someone lit a fire in me / Burn” — “Light a fire in me” normally means awakening passion/motivation. With the Devil present, fire also becomes Hell/fire. The positive idiom becomes sinister.

“stomach churning / … yearning” — Ren simultaneously feels revulsion and attraction. His body warns him while his desire pulls him toward the man. That's essentially the temptation mechanism of the whole song.
“I reached out my hand, he shook it” — Looks like an innocent handshake, but it's effectively the first agreement/deal before the literal contract appears. Foreshadows signing his soul away.
“Is it fame or fortune you aspire?” — The Devil immediately identifies the classic artist temptations: recognition and money. This is where the music-industry reading becomes especially strong.

“Follow me, I'll walk you through the fire” — Usually “walk through fire” means enduring hardship for someone. But who's offering to guide him? The Devil. Fire therefore simultaneously means adversity and Hell.

“every type of flavoring / budget of the catering / … taste that you've been savoring” — A whole food/taste scheme: flavoring → catering → taste → savoring. The Devil packages damnation like a salesman offering exactly what the customer has been craving.

“I don't want to come off as a salesman” — While delivering what is quite literally a sales pitch followed by a contract. Also fuels the record-label interpretation: fame, fortune, budget, salesman, signature.
“Let your pain go / Let the flames grow” — Clever contradiction: he's offering relief from suffering while simultaneously feeding the flames that will ultimately consume/enslave Ren.
“I know you got a name so / … write it on this line” — Starts sounding like asking someone's name, then reveals that he wants their signature. A very smooth transition from conversation to contract.

“Here, I got a pen and everything” — Almost comically mundane after all the supernatural imagery. The Devil isn't asking for a ritual—he has paperwork ready. Again fits both Faustian bargain and record contract.

“Who needs a wedding ring? I offer the divine” — A contract becomes almost a marriage/covenant. A wedding binds two people; this signature binds Ren to the Devil. “Divine” is also ironic coming from a fallen angel.
“I promise that you will in time” — The nasty part of the contract: Ren doesn't fully understand the terms before signing, but he'll understand the consequences afterward.
“crossroads of time” — Upgrades the physical crossroads into a life-changing decision point: after signing, his life divides into before/after.
“I leant down to sign” — Literally bending toward the paper, but visually/symbolically Ren is also moving downward toward the Devil/Hell. A possible visual wordplay rather than certain intent.
